header.userPrompt:
Simplify the bank-statements list page (`web/.../components/pages/BankStatementsPage.scala`) to always show one account's statements as a continuous timeline, instead of a flat multi-account list that hides fully-imported statements. This is a web-only change. No backend, API, model, or database changes.

## Background
The page fetches all of the user's bank statements on load (`GetBankStatements`, each statement has `id, bankName, productType, accountLast4, periodStart, periodEnd, createdAt, totalRows, processedRows, documentFilename, ...`). Today, with no account selected it renders a flat, paged list that hides fully-processed statements (every row imported or ignored) behind a "Show all" toggle; only when an account is selected does it render a single-account timeline with period ordering and a "gap" warning between missing cycles. Hiding statements makes a stored-but-hidden statement look like a missing cycle, which is the bug being fixed. The fix is to drop the multi-account/hide behavior entirely and always show a single selected account's full timeline.

## Required behavior
1. **An account is always selected; there is no "all accounts" mode.**
   - On load, default the selection to the account that owns the most recently uploaded statement (the one with the greatest `createdAt`). If there are no statements, there is nothing to select and the page shows its existing empty state.
   - The account picker (the existing `Account` select) stays, but its "All accounts" option is removed. Each option is one account, keyed by the existing `accountKeyOf` (`bankName~productType~accountLast4`).
   - Each option's label is `bankName (productType) ••••accountLast4`, e.g. `BBVA (Credit) ••••8927` — the bank name, then the human product type in parentheses, then the masked last four. Use the existing `productLabel` for the type wording. Update `accountLabelOf` to this format.
2. **Always render the single-account timeline** for the selected account: its statements sorted by period, newest first, with a gap warning (`gapWarning`, keep as-is) shown between two adjacent statements whenever a whole cycle appears to be missing between them. Keep the existing per-statement status indicator: "All done" when `processedRows == totalRows`, otherwise "N pending". No statement is ever hidden.
3. **Remove the now-dead UI and logic:**
   - the "Show all / Show pending only" toggle and the processed-hiding filter (`showAll` state, the `afterShowAll` filter),
   - the sort toggle (`sortBy` / `cycleSortBy`) — ordering is fixed to period, newest first,
   - paging (`page` state, `PageSize`, `totalPages`, the slice, and the pager controls at the bottom),
   - the flat non-account list branch (the `accountView == false` paths),
   - the **Type** filter dropdown (an account already fixes bank + product + last4).
   Keep the "Filter by name" (`stmtFilter`) box, applied within the selected account.
   Preserve the existing drafts/processing section at the top, the polling behavior, the delete handler, and navigation to a statement's review page.

## Tests
- Extract the default-account selection into a pure, testable helper (e.g. in a `BankStatementsLogic` object or similar), and unit-test it: the account of the statement with the newest `createdAt` is chosen; ties and an empty list behave sensibly (empty -> none). Follow the frontend testing conventions in `docs/guide/testing.md`.
- Update or remove any existing spec that assumed the old paging, "show all" hiding, or multi-account flat list.

## Out of scope
No changes to statement parsing, the review page, refunds, or any server code. Keep existing reviewer and commit-message conventions. Keep the page reachable exactly as it is now (same route and entry points).

resultJson.description:
The bank-statements list page (`web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementsPage.scala`, component `BankStatementList`) currently has two modes. With no account selected it shows a flat, paged, sortable multi-account list that hides fully-processed statements behind a "Show all" toggle. With an account selected it shows a period-ordered timeline with gap warnings. Because hidden statements look like missing cycles, users get false "gap" impressions. This epic removes the multi-account mode completely, so the page always shows one account's full timeline and never hides a statement.

After the change an account is always selected. By default it is the account that owns the statement with the greatest `createdAt`. The user can switch accounts with the existing `Account` select, which no longer has an "All accounts" option. Options are labelled like `BBVA (Credit) ••••8927`. The selected account's statements are sorted by `periodStart` newest first, with `gapWarning` placed between adjacent statements, and each card keeps its "All done" / "N pending" indicator. The "Filter by name" box still filters within the account. These are all removed: the Show-all toggle and processed-hiding filter, the sort toggle, paging and the pager, the Type filter, and the flat-list branch.

This is a web-only change: no server, API, model or DB changes. The drafts/import section, polling, delete, navigation to `/bank-statements/:id`, the route and the entry points all stay as they are. The default-account choice moves into a pure helper object so it can be unit-tested without the DOM, following RULE-TE-010.

tasks.description: Create `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementsLogic.scala`, a pure object with no React/MUI (doc comment in the style of `BankStatementReviewLogic`). Add `def defaultAccountKey(stmts: List[GetBankStatements.Response.BankStatement]): Option[String]`. It returns `BankStatementList.accountKeyOf` of the statement with the greatest `createdAt` (`maxByOption(_.createdAt)`: on a tie the first statement in list order wins, and an empty list gives None). In `BankStatementsPage.scala`, change `BankStatementList.accountLabelOf` to `s"${s.bankName} (${productLabel(s.productType)}) ••••${s.accountLast4}"`. Add `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementsLogicSpec.scala` (AnyWordSpec, must-matchers, a `stmt(...)` factory like the one in BankStatementListSpec but with a `createdAt` param). Cases: newest createdAt picks its account even when that statement is not first in the list; empty list -> None; tie -> first in list order. In `BankStatementListSpec`, add an `accountLabelOf` case asserting `BBVA (Credit) ••••8927` (and a non-credit/debit product type passing through). Verify: `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementsLogicSpec *BankStatementListSpec"`.

tasks.title: Make BankStatementList always render the selected account's full timeline
tasks.description: Rewrite the list portion of `BankStatementList.component` in `BankStatementsPage.scala`. (1) Keep the `accountFilter` state but default it via derivation: `val selectedAccount: Option[String] = Option(accountFilter).filter(k => accounts.exists(_._1 == k)).orElse(BankStatementsLogic.defaultAccountKey(localStmts))`. This also covers async loads, polling updates, and deleting the last statement of the chosen account. (2) Account select: `.value(selectedAccount.getOrElse(""))`, options are just `accounts` (drop the `"" -> "All accounts"` entry), each keyed with `.withKey(k)`, and onChange only calls `setAccountFilter`. Keep it rendered only when `accounts.nonEmpty`. (3) Displayed statements: filter `localStmts` to `selectedAccount`, apply the `stmtFilter` name filter, then `sortBy(_.periodStart.toEpochDay).reverse`. (4) Always interleave `gapWarning` between adjacent cards. (5) Delete `showAll`, `sortBy`/`cycleSortBy`, `page`/`setPage`, `PageSize`, `totalPages`, the slice, the `mui.Pagination` block (with its js.Dynamic), the Type select and `typeFilter`, and every `accountView` branch. `updateFilter` becomes just `setStmtFilter` (or inline it). Remove imports that become unused. `js` is still needed for `Int8Array`/`ArrayBuffer` in upload, so check before removing it. Leave drafts, upload, polling, delete, toast, card rendering and the 'All done'/'N pending' indicator untouched. If there are no statements, nothing is selected and the list is simply empty, as it is today. Verify with `CI=true sbt Test/compile` (-Werror catches unused imports/vals) and `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementListSpec *BankStatementsLogicSpec"`.

resultJson.brief:
Scope: web only (`web/` Scala.js + Slinky + MUI 5 via `com.olvind.mui.muiMaterial.components as mui`). Do not touch server/, lib/, or models.

Key files:
- `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementsPage.scala` holds two objects. `BankStatementsPage` is a thin wrapper: AsyncComponent fetches `ctx.api.client.getBankStatements` and renders `BankStatementList(ctx, stmts, onRefresh)`. `BankStatementList` is the real component, with these helpers: `productLabel(productType: String): String` ("credit"->"Credit", "debit"->"Debit", else passthrough); `accountKeyOf(s): String` = `s"${bankName}~${productType}~${accountLast4}"`; `accountLabelOf(s): String` (currently `bank · Product · ••••last4`); `metadataLine(s)`; `gapWarning(newer, older): Option[ReactElement]` (fires when `newer.periodStart - older.periodEnd > 20` days, keyed `gap-${older.id}`); and private `toListStmt` (used by polling).
- Inside the component: `localStmts` (Hooks.useState seeded from props, re-synced through `SafeHooks.useEffect(stmtsKey)`) is the source list, which polling and delete mutate. `accounts = localStmts.map(s => accountKeyOf(s) -> accountLabelOf(s)).distinctBy(_._1)`. Cards are built per statement with `.withKey(s.id.toString)`, and clicking a card when Parsed goes to `/bank-statements/${s.id}`. The filter row is a Box holding the Account select (`mui.TextField.outlined().select(true)...(mui.MenuItem.normal()(label).value(k).withKey(k).build ...*)`), the Type select, the name TextField, and the sort and show-all buttons. Pagination at the bottom uses js.Dynamic (banned by RULE-FE-014). Removing it is good, but `scala.scalajs.js` is still used by the upload code (`js.typedarray`).
- `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementListSpec.scala` contains pure tests of accountKeyOf and metadataLine, with a `stmt(...)` factory building `GetBankStatements.Response.BankStatement(id, documentFilename, documentStatus, bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4, periodStart: LocalDate, periodEnd: LocalDate, createdAt: java.time.Instant, totalRows, processedRows)`. No spec covers paging or show-all, so nothing needs deleting.
- Pattern to copy for the pure logic object: `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewLogic.scala` (`/** Pure logic behind ...: no React or MUI. */ object ...`).
- Route `/bank-statements` lives in `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/AppRouter.scala:87` and is unchanged.

Conventions:
- Hooks: use `SafeHooks.useEffect(key: String)` / `useMemo`, never raw deps on objects (RULE-FE-006). Prefer deriving the selected account over syncing it with an effect.
- Mapped elements need `.withKey`. Optional elements use `.fold[ReactElement](Fragment())`. No `js.Dynamic`/`asInstanceOf` in pages, except the pre-existing `e.target.asInstanceOf[dom.HTMLInputElement]` pattern, which is used throughout.
- Tests (docs/guide/testing.md): ScalaTest `AnyWordSpec` with `org.scalatest.matchers.must.Matchers.*` and `mustBe`. Spec files mirror source paths. `should` subjects name the method/behaviour, not the class (e.g. `"defaultAccountKey" should { "pick ..." in ... }`). Prefer pure-function tests and add no DOM tests (RULE-TE-010).
- Build: `CI=true` enables -Werror, so unused imports and locals fail compilation. Use targeted runs only: `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *Spec"` or `CI=true sbt Test/compile`, never the full `sbt test`. Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default shell node is v16 and yarn install fails). Format with `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`.
- No silent defaults: `defaultAccountKey` returns `Option`, and an empty list gives None (no fabricated key).
